# Requirements Quality Checklist: QR Session Sharing

**Purpose**: Validate that the QR session-sharing requirements are complete, clear, consistent, measurable, and ready for implementation.
**Created**: 2026-08-16
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are the availability, placement, and purpose of the `Show QR code` action defined for every valid waiting-room session? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001]
- [x] CHK002 Are the initial, on-demand, and post-selection QR presentation requirements all documented, including the absence of QR-related state before selection? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK003 Does the specification define all required QR presentation content and explicitly exclude duplicate-copy, download, export, and customization controls? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003]
- [x] CHK004 Are every required component of the canonical absolute join URL identified, including protocol, host or IP, optional port, base path, route, and encoded session identifier? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005]
- [x] CHK005 Are the requirements explicit that Copy link and QR sharing use one canonical URL result in every supported deployment shape? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006]
- [x] CHK006 Are all QR presentation states and lifecycle transitions documented, including idle, loading, ready, error, close, unmount, and reopen? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-009]
- [x] CHK007 Are bilingual content, accessibility, responsive behavior, and preservation of existing sharing and waiting-room behavior all represented as requirements rather than only as planned evidence? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007, Spec §FR-010, Spec §FR-011]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK008 Is “valid waiting-room session” defined precisely enough to determine when the QR action is available and when it is withheld? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK009 Is “public” origin distinguished clearly from the browser’s current origin, including the assumption about reachability by the scanning opponent? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, Spec §Assumptions and Clarifications]
- [x] CHK010 Are base-path normalization rules unambiguous for root, empty, leading-slash, trailing-slash, and already-prefixed values? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK011 Is “exactly the same absolute join URL” defined as a deterministic equivalence that includes encoding, path, protocol, host, and port? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, Spec §SC-002]
- [x] CHK012 Are “successfully generated and rendered QR code,” “fits without horizontal overflow,” and “narrow viewport” quantified or explicitly bounded enough for objective review without requiring pixel decoding? [Clarity, Spec §Compatibility and Boundary Requirements, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK013 Are the Close action, Escape dismissal, backdrop dismissal, and focus-restoration expectations stated consistently and without relying on unstated overlay behavior? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007, Spec §SC-004]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK014 Do the frontend-only scope, no-server decision, and planned dependency boundary agree without implying a new service contract, route, persistence mechanism, or external service? [Consistency, Spec §Out of Scope, Spec §Compatibility and Boundary Requirements, Plan §Summary]
- [x] CHK015 Do the absolute `/join` destination requirements remain consistent with the explicit statement that no new route or join-flow behavior is introduced? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005, Spec §Out of Scope]
- [x] CHK016 Do the requirements preserve the existing overlay contract while assigning only QR-specific state and content to the new presentation? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007, Spec §Compatibility and Boundary Requirements]
- [x] CHK017 Are the requirements for QR-unavailable or QR-unused situations consistent about preserving Copy ID, Copy link control/feedback, root-deployment destination compatibility, polling, and navigation while permitting only the configured-subpath canonical correction? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK018 Are translation-key parity, localized state messages, accessible names, and visible user-facing strings described as one consistent bilingual contract? [Consistency, Spec §FR-010, Spec §Compatibility and Boundary Requirements]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK019 Does SC-001 define the population of “valid waiting sessions” and the observable absence conditions needed to make its 100% and 0% targets meaningful? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-001]
- [x] CHK020 Does SC-002 specify a representative URL matrix covering hostname, IP address, non-default port, root path, and configured subpath, with an objective equality rule? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-002]
- [x] CHK021 Does SC-003 define exact opaque-ID transport/prefill separately from valid-UUID validation, without conflating a browser journey with physical QR scanning or broadening accepted join IDs? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-003]
- [x] CHK022 Does SC-004 make all three dismissal paths, focus restoration, and stale-result absence independently assessable? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-004]
- [x] CHK023 Do SC-005 through SC-007 distinguish localization parity, regression preservation, repository-gate completion, and unexpected delivery-artifact review as separate acceptance outcomes? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-005, Spec §SC-006, Spec §SC-007]

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK024 Are the primary on-demand sharing requirements complete from a valid waiting-room session through a ready QR presentation? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 1]
- [x] CHK025 Are alternate deployment scenarios covered for browser origins using a hostname, IP address, optional port, root path, and configured public subpath? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 2, Spec §SC-002]
- [x] CHK026 Are exception requirements complete for both QR-library failure and QR-generation failure, including the distinction between an error state and a successful QR result? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Spec §User Story 3, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK027 Are recovery requirements defined for close-while-pending, unmount-while-pending, and reopening with the current URL? [Coverage, Recovery Flow, Spec §FR-009, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK028 Are keyboard, assistive-technology, narrow-mobile, English, and Ukrainian scenarios treated as first-class requirements rather than optional presentation details? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 3, Spec §Compatibility and Boundary Requirements]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK029 Does the specification define the expected treatment of session identifiers containing characters that require query encoding? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK030 Are missing or invalid waiting-room session contexts tied to an explicit requirement for withholding the QR action and preserving the existing lifecycle authority? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK031 Are empty, root, duplicated, or dropped application base paths addressed as distinct boundary conditions for the canonical destination? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-005, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK032 Are pending, rejected, late, or failed QR results explicitly prevented from being described as a ready QR code? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-008, Spec §FR-009]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK033 Are dialog semantics, accessible title and description, status/error semantics, Close labeling, keyboard focus, and focus restoration specified for every QR presentation state? [Accessibility, contracts/ui.md §QR Sheet, Spec §FR-007]
- [x] CHK034 Are responsive requirements objectively reviewable across desktop and narrow mobile presentations, including the no-horizontal-overflow constraint? [Accessibility, Responsiveness, Spec §SC-004, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK035 Is the immediate presentation/loading expectation separated clearly from the absence of a numeric QR-generation-time target, so “immediate” cannot be interpreted inconsistently? [Performance, Spec §Compatibility and Boundary Requirements]
- [x] CHK036 Are privacy or security assumptions about exposing the session identifier in a shareable QR payload explicitly documented, even though authentication and authorization changes are out of scope? [Security, Spec §Out of Scope, Spec §Assumptions and Clarifications]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK037 Are the current waiting-room session identifier, canonical URL, and existing join-screen query handling identified as the authoritative sources for the share flow? [Dependency, Spec §Key Entities and State, Spec §Assumptions and Clarifications]
- [x] CHK038 Is the single application base-path setting documented as a dependency shared by asset delivery, routing, and join-URL construction, with ownership and precedence clear? [Dependency, Spec §Compatibility and Boundary Requirements, Spec §Assumptions and Clarifications]
- [x] CHK039 Are the approved browser-side QR-generation dependency and its failure boundary distinguished from observable product requirements, so implementation choices cannot silently expand scope? [Dependency, contracts/ui.md §Failure and lifecycle contract, Plan §Technical Context]
- [x] CHK040 Is the no-server-contract assumption paired with an explicit requirement to resolve or review any unexpected delivery-artifact change before implementation is considered ready? [Assumption, Spec §Compatibility and Boundary Requirements, Spec §Evidence and Documentation Impact]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
